business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 Business description
business_model.claim: Concentra is the largest provider of occupational health services in the United States by number of locations, selling workers' compensation injury care, employer services (physicals, drug and alcohol screening, vaccinations), and consumer health services to patients who are generally employed by employer customers across the country.
quotes: We were founded in 1979 and have grown to be the largest provider of occupational health services in the United States by number of locations.
Our patients are generally employed by our main customers — employers across the United States.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 7
business_model.claim: The company organizes its operations into three operating segments — occupational health centers, onsite health clinics, and other businesses — but reports them as a single reportable segment because of similar services, delivery process, target customers, and economic characteristics.
quotes: All three operating segments are aggregated into a single reportable segment in our consolidated financial statements based on similar services provided, service delivery process involved, target customers, and similar economic characteristics.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 7 revenue-by-segment table
business_model.claim: For the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 93% of the company's $2,163.4 million revenue came from occupational health centers, approximately 5% from onsite health clinics, and approximately 2% from other businesses.
quotes: For the year ended December 31, 2025 our revenue was $2,163.4 million, with approximately 93% from occupational health centers, approximately 5% from onsite health clinics, and approximately 2% from other businesses.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 7 operating statistics table and narrative
business_model.claim: Revenue growth is driven by two primary volume-and-rate levers: total patient visits (measured as visits per day, or VPD) and revenue per visit; in 2025 total OHC visits rose 7.3% to 13,546,707 and total VPD rose 7.7% to 53,124.
quotes: Our total patient visits increased 7.3% to 13,546,707 for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to 12,623,503 visits for the year ended December 31, 2024.
Total VPD volume increased 7.7% to 53,124 for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to 49,311 VPD for the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to the acquisition of Nova.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 7 narrative and operating statistics table
business_model.claim: Revenue per visit in the OHC segment increased 4.3% to $147.42 in 2025, with workers' compensation per-visit revenue up 5.3% to $210.15 (driven by state fee schedule increases) and employer services per-visit revenue up 2.7% to $92.84 (driven by negotiated rate increases).
quotes: Revenue per visit increased 4.3% to $147.42 for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $141.30 for the year ended December 31, 2024.

Revenue per visit for workers' compensation visits increased 5.3% to $210.15 from $199.53 and revenue per visit for employer services visits increased 2.7% to $92.84 from $90.36, for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 (industry description) and Item 1A (risk factors)
business_model.claim: Workers' compensation reimbursement is determined by state fee schedules or UCR guidelines set by state regulators, while employer services are priced through market-based negotiations with employers or third-party administrators; the company does not control either pricing mechanism.
quotes: The cost of medical care provided for workers' compensation services is generally determined by either a state fee schedule or usual, customary, and reasonable ("UCR") guidelines, based on the relevant regulations.

In our employer services business, while we can directly set the price for these services, the market rates for this portion of our business are substantially lower than the fees we receive for workers' compensation services.

business_model.claim: Cost of services, exclusive of depreciation and amortization, was the largest cost component at $1,550.3 million or 71.7% of revenue in 2025, down 50 basis points from 72.2% in 2024 due to staffing efficiencies relative to 13.9% revenue growth.
quotes: Cost of services was $1,550.3 million, or 71.7% of revenue, for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $1,372.2 million, or 72.2% of revenue, for the year ended December 31, 2024. The percentage of revenue decreased primarily due to increased staffing efficiencies, relative to a 13.9% increase in revenue during the period.

business_model.claim: General and administrative expense was $203.3 million or 9.4% of revenue in 2025, up from $156.3 million or 8.2% in 2024, driven by Nova and Pivot acquisition and transition costs, one-time Select separation costs, stock compensation, and new standalone personnel.
quotes: Our general and administrative expense was $203.3 million, or 9.4% of revenue, for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $156.3 million, or 8.2% of revenue, for the year ended December 31, 2024. The increase in general and administrative expense as a percentage of revenue is principally due to Nova and Pivot Onsite Innovations acquisition and transition costs, one-time costs to separate from Select, stock compensation expense, and the planned addition of new full-time employees and other personnel costs to support the separation from Select and operate as a standalone public company.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 Significant Events and Item 7; M&A pipeline comment from P6 investor presentation
business_model.claim: Acquisitions are a key top-line growth lever: in 2025 the company acquired Nova Medical Centers (67 occupational health centers, $265.0 million purchase price) and Pivot Onsite Innovations (over 240 onsite clinics, $54.4 million purchase price), adding 72 centers to the OHC network and expanding onsite locations to over 400.

competitive_position.basis: Stated as a risk factor in 10-K Item 1A (P2).
competitive_position.claim: A principal competitive threat is that Concentra may fail to compete effectively with other occupational health centers, onsite health clinics, hospitals, urgent care facilities, and telemedicine providers in the local markets it serves.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 industry-trends section; risk of workforce composition shift stated in P2.
growth_thesis.claim: U.S. workforce growth is a macro tailwind: the non-farm workforce reached 159.4 million employees at end-2025, up 6% from 2019, and the company cites reshoring of manufacturing, an aging workforce with more severe injuries, and rising comorbidities as structural drivers of demand. For this tailwind to persist, U.S. labor-force participation must not fall materially, industrial and construction employment must be sustained by reshoring, and injury/illness incidence must not decline due to safety improvements.

As the employed population continues to age, injuries for older workers are typically more severe and take longer to recover from
